title: Two Neighbors Start a Balcony Vegetable Garden
script: Yuni: [warmly] Dina, I saw you carrying pots up the stairs again. Are you finally starting that balcony garden you mentioned last month?
Dina: Yes, although I honestly have no idea what I'm doing yet. I bought seeds because they looked cheap and easy at the store.
Yuni: [concerned] What did you buy? Something simple, I hope, since neither of us has grown anything before.
Dina: Chili peppers and a small tomato plant. The shop owner said they don't need much space, so they should be fine on a small balcony.
Yuni: [honestly] That actually sounds manageable. Why did you decide to start now, after living here for three years without one plant?
Dina: Because vegetables at the market keep getting more expensive, and because I wanted something to take care of besides my job.
Yuni: [relieved] That makes sense. My mother always said a garden teaches you patience, even a tiny one on a balcony like ours.
Dina: I could use more patience, honestly. I get frustrated when things don't happen immediately.
Yuni: [thoughtful] Then this might be good for you. Nothing grows quickly, no matter how often you check the soil.
Dina: Since your mother taught you, could you tell me how much water these plants actually need each day?
Yuni: [reflective] Not too much, actually. Water needs vary. Check the plant type, drainage, weather, and soil below the surface instead of following one fixed daily amount.
Dina: I assumed more water would always help, but the roots also need air and good drainage. That's clearly wrong then.
Yuni: [peacefully] Most beginners think that. I made the same mistake with my first plant, and it died within two weeks.
Dina: Good thing I asked before I drowned these poor tomatoes on their first day here.
Yuni: [encouraging] Exactly. If you want, I can check on them with you sometimes, since I already water my own herbs every morning anyway.
Dina: I would really appreciate that. Maybe we could compare our balconies in a few months and see whose plants survived.
Yuni: Deal. Although honestly, I hope we're both still laughing about this, not mourning dead tomato plants.

quiz.question: What did Danu buy to start his balcony garden?
options: Chili peppers and a small tomato plant
Only flowers
A large fruit tree
Rice seeds
quiz.explanation: Danu bought chili peppers and a small tomato plant because the shop owner said they don't need much space.

quiz.question: Why did Danu decide to start gardening now?
options: His landlord required it
He won a gardening contest
Vegetables kept getting more expensive and he wanted something to care for
Yuni forced him to
quiz.explanation: He explains vegetables at the market keep getting more expensive, and he wanted something to take care of besides his job.

quiz.question: What does Yuni warn Danu about watering?
options: Water as much as possible every day
Never water the plants at all
Overwatering kills more plants than people expect
Only water at night
quiz.explanation: Yuni warns that overwatering kills more plants than expected, so he should water only when the soil feels dry.

quiz.question: What happened to Yuni's first plant?
options: It grew perfectly
She gave it away
Nothing, she never had one
It died within two weeks from overwatering
quiz.explanation: Yuni admits she made the same overwatering mistake with her first plant, and it died within two weeks.

quiz.question: What do Yuni and Danu agree to do?
options: Stop gardening completely
Check on the plants together and compare balconies in a few months
Sell their plants
Move to a bigger apartment
quiz.explanation: Yuni offers to check on the plants with him, and they agree to compare their balconies in a few months.

quiz.question: What two motivations bring Dina to gardening?
options: Winning a balcony contest and selling seeds
Yuni’s demand and free soil
A plan to replace market vegetables completely
Rising food prices and wanting a non-work responsibility
quiz.explanation: The garden has both practical and personal value.

quiz.question: Why might the selected plants suit a balcony?
options: They can grow in containers with adequate conditions
They never need sunlight
They produce food in a week
They cannot be overwatered
quiz.explanation: Space suitability does not remove other care needs.

quiz.question: What should guide watering?
options: A fixed daily amount for every pot
The appearance of dry leaves alone
The wish to make plants grow faster
Plant type, pot drainage, weather, and soil below the surface
quiz.explanation: The revision avoids one universal rule.

quiz.question: What does Yuni’s failed first plant contribute?
options: Proof that beginners should not garden
A concrete warning learned from experience
A reason to avoid tomatoes
Evidence that water is harmful
quiz.explanation: The failure supports more careful observation.

quiz.question: How does their agreement improve learning?
options: Yuni takes full control of Dina’s pots
They promise every seed will grow
They stop asking the shop owner
They can compare observations without turning survival into competition
quiz.explanation: Shared checking makes mistakes and patterns easier to notice.
